item.title: Pudu Robotics Unveils D5 Robot Dog, Aims for Global Expansion
item.description: A pale-grey, nearly one-metre-tall, four-legged robot drew crowds at Tokyo’s International Robot Exhibition, lowering itself down some steps before lifting its right foreleg as if to greet onlookers, and then rolled around one of the exhibition halls on wheels while avoiding obstacles. The quadruped, dubbed the D5, is the latest model unveiled on Wednesday by Chinese robot maker Pudu Robotics at IREX. IREX is a biennial industry showcase held at Tokyo Big Sight from Dec. 3 to 6. item.title: Online Retailers Courts, Prism+ Cited for Unfair Trade Practices
item.description: The Competition Commission of Singapore (CCS) has taken Courts and Prism+ to task over unfair practices. The consumer watchdog stated the electronics and home appliance retailers used misleading website design features. Credit: Courts Singapore (left), Facebook/Prism+ (right) CCS found that Courts automatically added unsolicited items to consumer shopping carts. item.title: Paramount Launches USD 108.4 Billion Hostile Bid for Warner Bros Discovery
item.description: Paramount Skydance has launched a hostile bid valued at USD 108.4 billion for Warner Bros Discovery. The move is a last-ditch effort to outbid Netflix and create a media powerhouse. It aims to challenge the dominance of the streaming giant.

item.title: Australia Enforces World-First Social Media Ban for Under-16s
item.description: Australia has implemented a world-first social media ban for children under 16, restricting access to platforms including TikTok, YouTube, Instagram, and Facebook. Ten major social media platforms were ordered to block underage children or face fines of up to A$49.5 million (USD 33 million). Prime Minister Anthony Albanese called it "a proud day" for families, framing the law as evidence policymakers can curb online harms. item.title: AI Poised to Boost Productivity, Impact Jobs at US Banks
item.description: US bank executives state that artificial intelligence will enhance productivity within their organisations, a development expected to lead to job reductions. JPMorgan Chase and Wells Fargo are among the banks discussing AI's influence. Credit: JPMorgan Marianne Lake, JPMorgan Chase's consumer and community banking chief, noted the bank has doubled productivity to 6% with AI, up from a prior 3% without it. item.title: Tencent Exits Paramount Bid for Warner Bros Amid US Regulatory Concerns
item.description: Chinese social media and gaming company Tencent Holdings has withdrawn as a financing partner from Paramount Skydance's USD 108 billion bid to acquire Warner Bros Discovery. This decision follows concerns about heightened scrutiny of foreign investment in the United States. Credit: TENCENT Warner Bros had expressed concern that Tencent's involvement as a non-US equity financer might prompt a review by the Committee on Foreign Investment in the United States (CFIUS). item.title: South Korea Mandates AI Ad Labeling Amid Surge in Deepfake Deception
item.description: South Korea is moving to address the surge of deceptive promotions created using artificial intelligence.

item.title: Chinese Xreal Powers Google’s Next Generation of AI Smart Glasses
item.description: Chinese augmented reality startup Xreal has formed a partnership with Google on Project Aura, a new venture aiming to launch AI glasses next year. Project Aura will be powered by the Android XR operating system and the Gemini AI model. Google initially announced Project Aura, which physically resembles a pair of thick sunglasses, at its annual I/O developer conference in May.

item.title: Disney and OpenAI Forge USD$1 Billion AI Partnership, Licensing Characters for Generative AI
item.description: Walt Disney has announced a three year partnership with OpenAI, committing to a $1 billion investment while simultaneously licensing its globally recognised characters for use in the startup’s Sora AI video generator. This deal, unveiled on December 11th, allows the AI tools to utilise characters from major franchises including Star Wars, Pixar, and Marvel, marking a pivotal moment in Hollywood’s reluctant yet necessary embrace of generative artificial intelligence.
